items.title: Adaptive protocol stabilizes bistable qubits using single-shot measurement
items.original_title: Operating a bistable qubit
authors: Fabrizio Berritta, Jan A. Krzywda, Tom Dvir, Paul Buttles, Stanislav Eilhart, Jeroen Danon, Ferdinand Kuemmeth
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Defects in solid-state quantum processors can interact with qubits, causing discrete frequency shifts that make them unstable and bistable. Researchers experimentally demonstrated an adaptive control protocol powered by a field-programmable gate array to correct these shifts using a single measurement. The approach successfully suppressed instabilities in a superconducting qubit, achieving significant error reduction and stabilizing gate fidelities over time.
items.why: Mitigating dephasing errors from defects is crucial for improving the performance and stability of large quantum processor arrays.
technical_details: The 1-bit feedback protocol reaches the information limit set by the qubit's intrinsic entropy.
Researchers deployed the protocol to achieve an estimation bandwidth of approximately 136 kHz and a 77% error reduction.
items.selection_reason: Demonstrates an adaptive FPGA-based feedback protocol to operate a bistable superconducting qubit suffering from TLS defects.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Adaptive protocol stabilizes bistable qubits using single-shot measurement

items.title: Training AI Agents to Automate Model Post-Training
items.original_title: Training LLM Agents to Automate LLM Post-Training with RSI-Dojo
authors: Shuzheng Gao, Zhaojian Yu, Penghao Yin, Yuling Shi, Kai Cai, Shilin He, Michael R. Lyu
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Researchers introduced an automated pipeline and collection of training environments designed to teach artificial intelligence agents how to conduct model post-training. The approach converts human research artifacts into executable environments, filtering tasks by execution reliability and data size to build a seed collection. Fine-tuning models on these collected trajectories improved their performance on standardized post-training benchmarks, matching the results of several frontier models.
items.why: Automating recursive self-improvement and post-training capabilities allows AI systems to more independently select data, diagnose failures, and enhance future model versions.
technical_details: The resulting models, RSI-Dojo-9B and RSI-Dojo-35B-A3B, improved over their base models by 8.74 and 16.87 PostTrainBench points respectively.
items.selection_reason: Demonstrates recursive self-improvement fine-tuning on Qwen models, improving post-training benchmark scores.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Training AI Agents to Automate Model Post-Training

items.title: Mapping Three-Dimensional Dark Matter Distribution Using Space Telescope Imaging
items.original_title: 3D dark matter map of the JWST COSMOS-Web field using diffusion-based generative priors
authors: Diana Scognamiglio, Brandon Zhao, Katherine L. Bouman, Olivier Dor\'e, Caitlin M. Casey, Maximilien Franco, Ghassem Gozaliasl, David Harvey, Olivier Ilbert, Jeffrey B. Jewell, Jeyhan S. Kartaltepe, Anton M. Koekemoer, Gavin Leroy, Richard Massey, Jason Rhodes, Brant E. Robertson, Marko Shuntov, Sune Toft, Greta Toni, Michael A. Troxel
items.continuity_note: Not included in the recent archived briefings.
items.summary: Researchers mapped the three-dimensional distribution of invisible matter, known as dark matter, across a specific sky region using deep space telescope imaging. By combining a physical lensing model with advanced generative computer models trained on cosmological simulations, the team reconstructed matter distributions across twenty distinct depth planes. This approach successfully separates overlapping cosmic structures and extends mapping capabilities to higher redshifts, reaching closer to a major epoch of rapid galaxy growth.
items.why: This technique extends three-dimensional weak lensing mapping into the high-redshift regime, enabling probabilistic visualization of the evolving cosmic web. It provides a robust route for tracing the growth of cosmic structure with current wide-field surveys.
technical_details: The reconstruction achieves an effective source density of 121 galaxies per square arcminute across the COSMOS-Web field.
It utilizes a diffusion-based Bayesian generative prior to yield a posterior distribution of the matter field to z approximately 2.
items.selection_reason: Reconstructs 3D dark matter distributions from JWST imaging using diffusion-based generative priors and weak lensing.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Mapping Three-Dimensional Dark Matter Distribution Using Space Telescope Imaging

items.title: Researchers Fabricate Free-Standing Two-Dimensional Metal Oxide Monolayers
items.original_title: Free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit
items.continuity_note: No material new development could be established from available evidence.
items.summary: Materials scientists have achieved the controlled fabrication of diverse free-standing two-dimensional metal oxides down to the single-atomic-layer limit. The team used an electron-beam-induced removal of halogen atoms from layered metal oxyhalides to transform the materials into ultrathin metal oxides. Analysis of monolayer chromium oxide confirmed thermodynamic stability and predicted magnetic ordering below a specific cryogenic temperature.
items.why: This atomic-scale synthesis technique creates stable monolayer oxide lattices and lateral heterostructures, opening new pathways for exploring quantum phenomena and excitonic properties in low-dimensional materials.
technical_details: The conversion relies on ionization-driven halogen selective removal and lattice relaxation from layered precursors like CrOCl to CrO.
Monolayer chromium oxide domains exceeded 10 4 nm 2 with predicted Néel antiferromagnetic order below 230 K.
items.selection_reason: Reports controlled fabrication of free-standing 2D metal oxides at the single-atomic-layer limit, highly relevant to nanoscale devices and materials research.
items.corroboration: Single substantive source; independent corroboration not established.
items.display_title: Researchers Fabricate Free-Standing Two-Dimensional Metal Oxide Monolayers
